scope.q: What specific KPIs are we optimizing for (e.g., total distance per order, average picking time, order throughput), and what are the target improvements?
scope.why: This defines the objective function for any analysis or optimization, and clarifies what 'too far' means in measurable terms.

scope.q: What WMS data fields are consistently captured for each pick, including item location, picker ID, timestamps, and actual path taken, and is it accessible via API or database?
scope.why: Data availability and granularity are foundational; this determines if we can reconstruct paths accurately and what insights are extractable.

scope.q: Are we only analyzing historical data to identify inefficiencies, or is the scope also to generate optimized picking routes and/or suggest warehouse layout changes?
scope.why: This clarifies the expected deliverables: a diagnostic report versus a prescriptive system with actionable, live recommendations.

decomposition.title: WMS Data Integration & ETL
decomposition.why: We need to reliably extract raw WMS data and transform it into a clean, structured format for analysis.

decomposition.title: Picker Path Reconstruction & Analytics
decomposition.why: This involves re-creating picker movements from raw data to calculate distances and identify common, inefficient patterns.

decomposition.title: Warehouse Layout & Item Affinity Modeling
decomposition.why: Understanding the physical layout and how items are co-picked is crucial for identifying re-slotting opportunities.

decomposition.title: Route Optimization & Simulation Engine
decomposition.why: Developing an algorithm to generate more efficient picking paths and quantify their potential impact is a core deliverable.

decomposition.title: Performance Dashboard & Recommendation Interface
decomposition.why: Results need to be visualized and actionable recommendations presented to the warehouse operators effectively.

risks.risk: WMS data quality and granularity are insufficient for accurate path reconstruction or item location mapping.
risks.mitigation: Conduct a thorough data audit upfront, including sample data review with warehouse operations, to identify missing fields or inconsistencies; implement data validation checks during ingestion.

risks.risk: Warehouse layout changes frequently or is not consistently reflected in WMS data, making optimization models outdated.
risks.mitigation: Establish a clear process for automatic or manual updates of warehouse layout data; design the system to handle dynamic layout changes gracefully, perhaps by versioning layouts.

risks.risk: Picker behavior is highly variable and doesn't always follow 'optimal' paths for reasons not captured in data (e.g., ad-hoc tasks, equipment issues).
risks.mitigation: Involve pickers and supervisors in the design and validation phases to understand practical constraints; incorporate 'human factors' into optimization by allowing flexible pathing or feedback loops.

risks.risk: The proposed optimization strategies (route changes, re-slotting) are met with resistance from warehouse staff or disrupt existing workflows too much.
risks.mitigation: Start with small-scale pilot programs and A/B testing in controlled environments; demonstrate clear benefits and involve key stakeholders early to build buy-in and gather feedback from the ground up.
